hints: Focus on the type of bonding in aluminium chloride, is it really ionic with $\text{Al}^{3+}$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions or is it covalent molecular?
Remember that $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ is a dimer with 4 terminal Cl atoms and 2 bridging Cl atoms joining the two Al centres together.
Think about who supplies both electrons in the bridge bonds, and check which diagram shows terminal shared pairs plus dative bridges with no direct Al-Al bond.
walkthrough:
**Decide ionic or covalent**

Aluminium chloride is covalent, not ionic. Al is in Group 13 with 3 outer electrons, Cl is in Group 17 with 7 outer electrons.

So we expect shared pairs, not $2[\text{Al}]^{3+} + 6[\text{Cl}]^-$:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6 \text{ is molecular, formula as dimer of } \text{AlCl}_3$$

**Draw the dimer structure**

Two $\text{Al}$ atoms are held together by two bridging Cl atoms. Each Al also has two terminal Cl atoms.

That gives 4 normal covalent Al-Cl bonds and 2 dative (coordinate) bridge bonds:
$$4 \times \text{ terminal Al-Cl (1e from Al + 1e from Cl)} + 2 \times \text{ bridge Cl } \rightarrow \text{ Al (2e from Cl)}$$

**Check electron origin and octets**

In a correct dot-and-cross, a terminal bond shows one cross ($\times$ from Al) overlapping one circle ($\text{o}$ from Cl). A bridge bond shows both electrons as circles from Cl donated to electron-deficient Al.

Only one diagram shows this pattern, with every Cl having 8 electrons, each Al surrounded by 8 shared electrons, and no Al-Al bond.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows ionic $2[\text{Al}]^{3+}$ and $6[\text{Cl}]^-$. $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ is a covalent dimer, not a giant ionic lattice. Al loses its 3 electrons by sharing, not by full transfer.
options.B: Correct. This shows 4 terminal Al-Cl covalent bonds with one $\times$ from Al and one $\text{o}$ from Cl shared, plus 2 bridging Cl atoms each donating both electrons (two $\text{o}$) datively to the two Al atoms. All Cl atoms have octets and each Al achieves 8 electrons in its shell with no Al-Al bond.
options.C: Incorrect. Although the shape looks like a bridged dimer, the electron source is reversed. It implies Al is donating to Cl in the bridges. In reality Al is electron deficient and the bridging Cl donates both electrons to Al by dative bonding.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows a direct Al-Al bond with shared crosses in the centre and only terminal Cl atoms. There is no Al-Al bond in $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$. The two Al centres are linked only through two bridging Cl atoms.
